findings.original_assumption: The variables belong to a commutative unital algebra.
findings.finding: The first-excluded-prefix identity uses only finite sums, products, zero and one; a commutative semiring suffices.
findings.proposed_revision: Let R be a commutative semiring, let t belong to R and let (u_x) be a family of elements of R. The same displayed identity holds.
findings.impact: Strengthens generality of article Lemma 5.1. Its application to signed-measure convolution algebras is unchanged. No change to constants, exponents or asymptotic claims.

findings.original_assumption: The original proof uses analytic square-root branches, a Cauchy estimate, a tail bound and a polynomial equality case.
findings.finding: Finite formal-series coefficients and separation of integer squares prove the same uniform bound U <= (64R)^d by an entirely algebraic argument.
findings.proposed_revision: Use D=2^d, A=DP and Q=D^2G-A^2. Formal coefficient cancellation gives degree Q <= k-1 and H(Q) <= (k+1)2^(5d)R^d <= (64R)^d. If Q(U) is nonzero, integer-square separation gives 2^k U^k <= |Q(U)| <= k H(Q) U^(k-1), hence U <= H(Q); the zero case follows from the integral-root height bound.
findings.impact: Proof simplification only. Retains real R >= 1, integer U >= 2R, distinct bounded integer shifts, all even degrees d >= 2, and the exact constant 64. No downstream exponent changes. No error in the original analytic inequalities is asserted.

findings.original_assumption: The combined lemma assumes B comparable to log N and H comparable to B, with fixed comparison constants.
findings.finding: The local bound needs only H=O(B) with B comparable to log N. The global and two-defect-window conclusions need only upper logarithmic bounds on H and window length, without the intermediate B. A lower comparison H comparable to B is unnecessary for all three conclusions, within the paper cutoff domain H >= 2.
findings.proposed_revision: Use H=O(B) for the local estimate, retaining B comparable to log N. State the global count uniformly for H <= D log N and integer counting height X <= CN, and the dyadic two-defect-window count uniformly for H <= D log N and L <= E log N, with fixed constants. All fixed real affine interval changes retain the conclusions.
findings.impact: Strengthens parameter scope in all three parts of T1.3, including fixed bounded cutoffs in the paper domain. No change to exponents 1/2 or 0 and no error in the original conclusion is asserted. The entire T1.3 lemma, including exact affine window geometry, is now proved.

validation_history.scope: Global and two-defect conclusions; no lower logarithmic cutoff required.
All three T1.3 conclusions with weaker cutoff hypotheses, literal B=L+1, independent component quantifiers and exact fixed real affine interval versions.

findings.original_assumption: U is comparable to N on both sides and B=O(log N); the general rank conclusion is stated for B asymptotic to c log N.
findings.finding: Only a fixed lower bound U>=aN is needed in every local-rigidity conclusion. For each fixed t and 0<c<2-2^(1-t), one threshold controls all bases U>=aN and all positive lengths B<=c log N. The upper base bound and the asymptotic lower comparison on B are unnecessary.
findings.proposed_revision: Fix a>0 and state local rigidity uniformly for U>=aN. For each fixed t and 0<c<2-2^(1-t), the relation rank is less than t uniformly for all positive B<=c log N. The finite Griesmer bound is uniform in every t after N, whereas t remains fixed before the asymptotic rank threshold.
findings.impact: Strengthens the local-rigidity domain to arbitrarily large bases and every shorter logarithmic window. The constant 64, critical coefficient 1/log 2, sharp rank thresholds and error exponents are unchanged. Actual infinite-model critical-band marginals remain p or 2p and satisfy the proved pointwise (2*2^C)/N bound.

findings.original_assumption: For B≥2, a nonempty even set I⊆[-B,B] with cardinality m, and x>(B+1)^(12m), the translated product is not an integer square.
findings.finding: The stronger threshold x>(64B)^m suffices, hence the simpler uniform threshold x>(B+1)^(5m) for B≥2. It follows directly from the proved degree-uniform algebraic split-product theorem.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace the exponent 12m by 5m, or state the sharper condition x>(64B)^m. Prove the result by the internal T1.1 bound with U=x and R=B; the threshold itself gives x≥2B.
findings.impact: Strengthens the finite local square exclusion. Distinct integer offsets, positive even m and the original domain B≥2 are retained. The original statement and all later exponents remain valid; no optimality of the new threshold is asserted.

findings.original_assumption: The number of 10B-defective positions in every critical window is O_C(B/log B). Companion T9.3 likewise states its free-component error as O_C(B/log B).
findings.finding: One positive absolute multiplicative constant works for every fixed critical-band width C. Only the eventual threshold N0 depends on C. The count is the actual kernel-one set in the full vertex interval. The free-component comparison in T9.3 also has an absolute multiplicative constant before C, with a C-dependent threshold, by the complete rank-cost proof and the critical local-kernel bound.
findings.proposed_revision: There exists an absolute K>0 such that for every fixed C there is N0(C), and all N≥N0(C), all critical-band lengths L and all dyadic starts x, the number of n∈V_x with K_(10B)(n)=1 is at most K B/log B, where B=L+1. In T9.3, the same quantifier order also gives an absolute constant for |c-d_xy|≤K B/log B, with only the threshold depending on C; the multiplicative constant need not equal the one in T9.2.
findings.impact: Clarifies and strengthens the constant uniformity in T9.2. The threshold may still depend on the fixed band width. No admissibility, positive start probability or full-rank assumption is added. The cutoff 10B and the B/log B rate are unchanged. This constant uniformity propagates to the full free-component estimate in T9.3, including overlapping physical windows. The two local kernels are bounded using the proved critical rigidity theorem; no regularity or admissibility premise is introduced.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T22.2 assumes regular windows, hence a common marginal p, and gives q(I)≤p·sum_x q(I\{x}) and the ordered-tuple bound RNp·E(Z_G)_(R-1).
findings.finding: The same missing-full-support condition gives q(I)≤sum_x p_x q(I\{x}) for arbitrary windows with their exact heterogeneous marginals, including incompatible events and zero marginals. If pmax≥0 bounds every actual marginal on G, the tuple sum is at most R|G|pmax·E(Z_G)_(R-1). Regularity is needed only to substitute the nominal p, and |G|≤N yields the original bound.
findings.proposed_revision: State the pointwise missing-block inequality with exact p_x on an arbitrary finite family. State its ordered-tuple consequence with |G| and any nonnegative upper bound pmax for the actual marginals. Then specialize to regular windows, pmax=p=2^(-L), and |G|≤N to recover the original assertion.
findings.impact: Extends the probability and tuple estimates to heterogeneous or irregular windows. It retains affine incompatibility and the exact structural missing-full-support premise. No independence, separation, positive-marginal filter, moment bound or cardinality cutoff is added. The original exponent and constant RNp are unchanged as a corollary.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T9.4 selects a primitive integer factor Q of a nonzero bivariate integer polynomial P, and also bounds its integer quotient.
findings.finding: Primitivity of Q is unnecessary. Every integer factorization P=Q*R with P nonzero gives the same exact bounds for both factors, with constant 2^(dX+dY) and the same sqrt((dX+1)(dY+1)) coefficient rectangle factor.
findings.proposed_revision: For every nonzero P in Z[X,Y] and every integer factorization P=Q R, both H(Q) and H(R) are at most 2^(dX+dY)||P||₂, which is at most 2^(dX+dY)sqrt((dX+1)(dY+1))H(P). Remove the primitive adjective; no separate content adjustment is needed.
findings.impact: Weakens a hypothesis without changing the original constants or partial-degree dependence. The proof uses univariate Mahler bounds and Parseval and includes degree-lowering specializations. The original primitive-factor conclusion is retained. No error in the manuscript conclusion or its multivariate proof is asserted.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T23.1 restricts the quadratic-reference parameter to 0≤a≤1 in the exact positive factorial-moment perturbation.
findings.finding: The same epsilon and the same pointwise factors and exact total variation formula hold on 0≤a≤2. The perturbation is nonzero for a<2; at a=2 it vanishes, and all moments agree. The uniform exponential-moment bound on the enlarged interval uses 1+(exp(t)-1)² instead of 1+(exp(t)-1)²/2. The original sharper bound is retained on [0,1].

Keep epsilon, the pointwise 1/2 and 3/2 factors, the factorial-moment difference and the exact TV formula. For a uniform exponential bound on 0≤a≤A≤2, use (3/2)exp(exp(t)-1)(1+(A/2)(exp(t)-1)²); A=1 recovers the original proof bound.
findings.impact: Weakens the parameter restriction without changing the original construction or distance constant. Equality of factorial moments occurs exactly off order m when a<2; the endpoint degeneracy is explicit. The enlarged uniform exponential constant is stated separately. The original range and all its conclusions remain proved. No error in the original statement and no optimality of an obstruction rate are claimed. The subsequent unnumbered m_N/Stirling argument is proved at a later separate checkpoint; the parameter extension alone is not used as a substitute for that proof.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T19.13 assumes mu>0 for the Poisson comparison and 0<mu,nu<=M for stability.
findings.finding: The Poisson comparison holds unchanged for mu>=0, including the actual point-mass reference at mu=0. Stability holds for every real mu and nu with upper bound 2(1+abs(mu))TV(P,Q)+abs(mu-nu). The source bound with M therefore needs only 0<=mu<=M; no positivity or upper bound on nu is needed.

findings.impact: Weakens only parameter hypotheses. All original constants and conclusions are retained. The reference Poisson law still requires mu>=0; only the recurrence norm and its stability admit negative parameters. Absolute convergence and the factorial resolvent are proved without a first-moment assumption, as already claimed in the source. No error in the original result is asserted.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T2.2 assumes natural K,d>=1 and uses the full number n of coordinate positions in its codimension bound.
findings.finding: The bound holds with n_plus, the number of coordinates whose forms are initially nonzero on R, in place of n. The construction and both final regularity properties hold for all natural K and d, including zero, with the same denominators K+1 and d+1 and exact codimension card(D).
findings.proposed_revision: Let n_plus count the initially nonzero coordinate forms with multiplicity and use n_plus/(K+1)+(s-r)/(d+1). Allow K,d>=0. The original statement follows from n_plus<=n; K=0 forces the final space to be zero, while d=0 forbids decompositions of a present nonzero form into two distinct present nonzero forms.

There is no claim that arbitrary later restrictions preserve regularity, and no error in the original result is asserted.

An unordered decomposition of the vertex label chooses two full coordinate-label classes, each of size at most K, so their product already covers both block assignments. More generally no three-block coloring is needed if each row support has size at most three; nonzero labels, zero row sums and the two regularity bounds suffice.

State the row-type and component conclusions for any family of supports of size at most three with zero label sum, after deleting zero labels and identifying repeated supports. The three-block situation is an immediate specialization.

The forms need not separate points. The codimension constant 2, literal parameter t^(-1/d) and original representation bound remain valid.

findings.original_assumption: The last clause of article Lemma 6.1 counts unordered representations by j distinct linearly independent labels with bound j!*t^(j-1), for 1<=j<=d.
findings.finding: The stronger bound j!*(t-1)^(j-1) holds. It also counts all zero-sum-free label supports of size j and fixed nonzero sum, rather than only linearly independent supports. The counting argument works in any abelian group when the stated absence of t disjoint nonempty sum representations holds.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace j!*t^(j-1) by j!*(t-1)^(j-1). Clarify the unordered-support convention used in the proof. The same bound can be stated for supports with no nonempty zero-sum subset, with the independent-support statement as a corollary.
findings.impact: Improves the finite constant and enlarges the counted class. A maximal disjoint family has at most t-1 members; its union is a transversal of size at most j*(t-1). Erasing a marked label gives a smaller zero-sum-free representation of a nonzero residual. The full recurrence and its factorial constant are proved. An ordered-tuple count would multiply the support count by j!; the source support convention is retained. No error or optimality claim is made.

findings.original_assumption: Article Lemma 7.1 assumes 1/2<sigma<1 and T>=1, in the surrounding regime Y>=B. Its companion proof bounds an infinite square-part series by zeta(2*sigma).
findings.finding: The bound holds at sigma=1/2 as well. For every real X,Y,T>=0 the actual positive-integer count is at most 2*sqrt(X)*sqrt(T)*exp(2*sqrt(Y)). More generally 1/2<=sigma<1 gives X^sigma*T^(1-sigma)/(1-sigma)*exp(Y^(1-sigma)/(1-sigma)), including the same real cutoffs. Thus the exponential constant may be fixed as 1/(1-sigma), independently of C1, and the prefactor at X=C1*N as C1^sigma/(1-sigma).
findings.proposed_revision: Allow 1/2<=sigma<1 and give the explicit constants. Count the finite square-part fibre directly by floor(sqrt(X/(k*s))) before the Rankin comparison; this avoids the divergent zeta(1) at the endpoint. State the more general Y,T>=0 version if useful, while retaining T>=1 and Y>=B in later applications.
findings.impact: Adds the square-root endpoint and explicit uniform constants. The original proof route via an enlarged infinite square-part sum does not reach that endpoint, but the finite fibre bound does. The original interior statement is a direct corollary. No error or optimality claim is made.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T22.3 has a factor zeta(2*sigma) for 1/2<sigma<1. Its logarithmic prime-budget estimate is uniform on [3/5,3/4] for Y>=3, with an O(1+Y^(1-sigma)/logY) remainder.

The logarithmic estimate holds uniformly for 1/2<=sigma<=3/4, X>=1 and Y>1, with remainder at most (65+4*log(4))*Y^(1-sigma)/logY. findings.impact: Strengthens both inequalities and their parameter ranges, with a single constant chosen before the finite prime set, exponent and cutoffs. The proof is elementary: the primorial bound controls all initial logarithmic prime sums; Abel comparison controls their power-weighted versions; a fixed 1/8 logarithmic loss gives the uniform unweighted prime sum. No PNT, zeta upper bound or unproved prime estimate is needed. No original conclusion is corrected, and no optimality claim is made.

The full count also only needs an upper logarithmic width bound B<=D*logN, without a critical-band lower bound. The threshold is uniform over every source tuple and every allowed length.

The finite code bound (B*sum of source-value divisor counts)^k can be recorded as an explicit intermediate estimate.
findings.impact: Relaxes the certificate threshold and length assumptions with unchanged asymptotic order. For a finite family of positive source values, each group selects a divisor and a target offset; coprimality and the product threshold give at most one target per code. Counting these independent divisor choices avoids an ordered-factorization estimate. All congruence and divisor estimates are proved internally. No original conclusion is corrected or optimality claim is made.

The second window may have local even square relations. The full at-most-one-common-root bound and removal of at most two equations, with squarefree remaining polynomials and disjoint roots, are proved in this broader setting.

findings.original_assumption: The source saturation relation uses a divisor D>6*N*B of the kernel product of two distinct anchor values.

The separately defined larger relation has outgoing degree at most B^2*(B+1)^m, incoming degree at most B^2*(2*exp(1)*B)^m, and the union of both neighborhoods at most twice the latter. findings.original_assumption: Article Lemma 7.4 bounds the admissible-set generating function by exp(M*z+4*n*Delta*z^2/(1-4*Delta*z)) for z>=0 and 4*Delta*z<1.
findings.finding: A disjoint-star partition proves the stronger bounds exp(M*z+n*z*((1+z)^Delta-1)) and exp(M*z+n*z*(exp(Delta*z)-1)) for every z>=0. A rational corollary is exp(M*z+2*n*Delta*z^2/(2-Delta*z)) under the wider Delta*z<2 condition. The fully heterogeneous version bounds the actual sum of products of nonnegative vertex weights by exp(sum_marked w_v + sum_v w_v*(prod_{u adjacent v}(1+w_u)-1)).

findings.original_assumption: The unnumbered correction-coefficient estimate states exp(-lambda)/4 <= C(lambda) <= 1, with C(lambda)=norm(Poisson(lambda)*Delta^2)/4 and lambda>0.
findings.finding: The lower bound can be doubled to exp(-lambda)/2 <= C(lambda). More generally, every summable real sequence of total mass zero has l1 norm at least twice any one of its coefficients. Applying this to the second Poisson difference and its positive mass exp(-lambda) at zero proves the stronger lower bound. The Lean result also includes lambda=0 for the signed-difference definition.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace the lower coefficient bound exp(-lambda)/4 by exp(-lambda)/2, keeping the original upper bound and all normalizations. Mention the zero-total-mass factor of two in the proof.
findings.impact: Improves only the explicit lower constant by a factor of two; the asymptotic exponents and normalization of total variation are unchanged. The original weaker estimate is true, so no manuscript error is asserted. The unnumbered inequality does not add a numbered coverage item.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T20.1 is stated in the ambient setting of three distinct regular windows with pairwise direct relative square-class spaces and cutoff H=C0*B for fixed C0>1.
findings.finding: The whole line-product estimate and its uniform offset-count conclusions need only first-window regularity and directness of the first and second square-class spaces. The second and third windows need no regularity, and the third space needs no directness condition. The cutoff may satisfy H>=B, including C0=1. The primitive direction and parametrization of every lattice point on the line are constructed internally.
findings.proposed_revision: State the line estimate under injectivity of the first even-selection map and directness with the second space, or retain first-window regularity as a convenient sufficient condition. Require only H>=B for canonical offsets. Keep stronger regularity/directness assumptions wherever later plane or residual-space arguments use them.
findings.impact: Weakens assumptions for the entire line estimate only. The third center may even coincide with another center in the stronger theorem; it still obeys the source size/positivity bounds. No later geometric lemma is asserted to inherit this extension automatically, and no manuscript error or optimality claim is made.

findings.original_assumption: T20.1 bounds the number of distinct offsets supplied by primes above Y by 1+log(6*N*B)/logY, with an O_{C0,C}(B/logB) estimate for this majorant.
findings.finding: The additive one is unnecessary: the actual distinct offset count is at most log(6*N*B)/logY for Y>=H>=B and large critical N. The original majorant itself is uniformly at most (1+6*log(2))*B/logB, with this absolute multiplicative constant chosen before the band constant, cutoff multiple, centers, line and Y. The threshold may depend on the fixed band constant; the uniform o(B) statement has its explicit epsilon quantifiers.
findings.proposed_revision: Remove the additive one from the distinct-offset bound and record that the logarithmic majorant permits an absolute multiplicative constant, for example 1+6*log(2) eventually. Retain the explicit threshold dependence and the order of quantifiers for the o(B) conclusion.
findings.impact: Sharpens the finite count and its parameter uniformity. The same whole-product bound 6*N*B covers the single-offset and multiple-offset cases, and the empty prime pool is included. The original weaker bound is true; no error or optimality claim is made.

findings.original_assumption: T20.3 is stated for three distinct regular windows with pairwise direct square-class spaces, with shared-prime cutoff H=C0*B and C0>1. Its mass conclusion is restricted to primitive triples.
findings.finding: The complete finite geometric conclusion needs only the first two windows to have full effective rank; pairwise directness of all three spaces is retained. The two-plane mass bound holds for the larger population in which only the first two starts are distinct, regular and direct: the third may be irregular, dependent or repeated. Its actual joint probability is at most p^2, and the uniform bound N^(-1+epsilon) follows. Canonical shared odd-valuation offsets need only H>=B. The subsequent-offset equation holds for every common integer divisor q>12*B^3, including composite q; the initial three-divisor product argument still uses distinct primes.
findings.proposed_revision: Weaken regularity in the forced-plane statement to two windows while retaining all pairwise directness hypotheses used to prove nonzero normal coordinates. State the two-plane mass estimate for any population with a first regular direct pair and a third start in the ambient interval. Allow H>=B for the canonical offsets, and mention the common-divisor extension of the subsequent-offset equation.
findings.impact: Extends precisely this forced-plane proposition and its two-plane mass estimate. No normal-budget, later covering or residual-space result is claimed under these weaker hypotheses. The original bounds remain true; no manuscript error or optimality claim is made.

findings.original_assumption: The last sentence of companion Proposition T19.2 bounds the total endpoint correction by 2*L*p, after counting at most two truncated local blocks.
findings.finding: The absolute correction of each nonempty clipped block is at most p*(card(fullBlock)-1). Consequently the total correction is at most p times the sum of these full lengths minus one over the actually truncated blocks, and in particular at most 2*(L-1)*p. The sharper bound holds in the full finite rank-one formulation and uniformly throughout every fixed critical band.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace 2Lp by 2(L-1)p in the endpoint correction, or give the finer bound p times the sum of card(fullBlock)-1 over the actual truncated blocks. Explain that every clipped block is nonempty and retains at least one full-block start.
findings.impact: Sharpens the finite boundary constant while keeping the same asymptotic order. It changes neither the exact Bernoulli parameter nor the mean and absolute discrepancy identities. It asserts no sign of the total mean bias and no optimality. The original weaker bound is true; no manuscript error is claimed.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T19.8 bounds the zero-coordinate fraction in the relation kernel by p*2^t and gives c(C)>=(1-card(C)*p*2^t)*q(C) after all integer private ranks are less than t.
findings.finding: The exact missing-coordinate fraction is 2^r_i/2^dim(S_i), where r_i is the actual private rank. Hence the general compatible lower bound retains the heterogeneous profile 1-sum_i 2^r_i/2^dim(S_i). In the source equal-rank setting, r_i<t implies r_i<=t-1, so the factor improves to 1-card(C)*p*2^(t-1). Every canonical direct component of the constructed terminal family inherits this stronger estimate. The exact remaining-rank deletion charge is also retained as t*(m-card(B))+rank(B)<=R.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace p*2^t by p*2^(t-1) in the positive-core comparison, and optionally state the sharper profile using all individual local dimensions and private ranks. Retain the actual remaining-rank term in the deletion budget when useful.
findings.impact: Halves the homogeneous loss factor and supplies a finite heterogeneous refinement. It does not assert that the displayed lower factor is always positive, nor does it supply a later arithmetic large-component construction. All original bounds remain true; no manuscript error or optimality claim is made.

findings.original_assumption: Companion T21.2 bounds the finite old-pool contribution to the conditional mean by p*2^(T-1)*B*card(poolValues), for 1<=T<=L.
findings.finding: The exact original conditional-mean bound holds with coefficient p*(2^(T-1)-1)/T. The conditional probability is exactly p when the supported value count t is at most one. For 2<=t<=T its excess over p is at most p*(2^(t-1)-1), whose ratio to t is bounded by (2^(T-1)-1)/T. Charging excess mass to the actual incidence budget sum_x t_x<=B*card(poolValues) proves the sharper coefficient. The finite refined theorem also admits T=0, with zero slope and the large-t population retained explicitly.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace p*2^(T-1) in the finite conditional-mean pool term by p*(2^(T-1)-1)/T and include the incidence-slope argument; keep the actual overlap and large-t terms.
findings.impact: Reduces the source pool coefficient by the factor (1-2^(1-T))/T for T>=1; it vanishes at T=1. This finite improvement by itself does not bound the large-t population. The separate fixed-j prime-pool asymptotic was subsequently closed, completing T21.2; the recorded validation commit below preserves the earlier finite improvement checkpoint. No original error or optimality claim is made.

findings.original_assumption: The original-window exceptional bound in T1.15 is j*(2L+1)+B*sqrt(3N)*exp(2sqrt(m_jN)), after deleting contacts and windows containing at least two old-pool-supported values.
findings.finding: For the original consecutive windows, the deterministic exception set need contain only starts with at least two old-pool-supported values. The actual conditional relative kernel vanishes whenever there is at most one such value, regardless of contact. The entire new relative vector is fair and independent of every old raw value under the original infinite prime-sign measure. Twice the number of exceptional starts is at most B*card(poolValues), yielding the stronger bound (B/2)*sqrt(3N)*exp(2sqrt(m_jN)), with no separate j*(2L+1) term. The literal source bound and uniform fixed-j exponent remain proved.
findings.proposed_revision: For the original-window branching statement, use the deterministic set of starts containing at least two pool-supported values, omit a separate contact deletion and replace the pool coefficient B by B/2. Include the full-vector conditional argument and the incidence count.
findings.impact: Removes an unnecessary finite contact term and halves the finite pool coefficient in the proved original-window scope. The full actual relative vector is fair and independent of all old raw values. No optimality or estimate for all arithmetic dependencies is claimed. Fixed dilations, subsets and enlarged-window variants were subsequently closed in the complete T1.15 implementation; the recorded validation commit preserves the earlier original-window improvement checkpoint. The same two-supported-value criterion was subsequently used to close T22.4 at growing critical orders, with its literal logarithmic correction and a proved uniform envelope; this does not assert growing-order moment bounds.

findings.original_assumption: The scalar recurrence comparison in T19.11 assumes 0<=theta<min(mu,1/2). Its size-bias identity is stated with theta=Var(X)-E(X), under that range.
findings.finding: For every mu>0 the same comparison holds for 0<=theta<=mu with theta<1/2, including the pure double-jump reference theta=mu. Its single Poisson intensity is then zero, and stationarity still holds. The exact size-bias identity in fact holds for every 0<=theta<=m, requiring only a positive finite first moment; theta need not be defined using a variance.
findings.proposed_revision: For mu>0 permit 0<=theta<=mu and theta<1/2 in the scalar comparison. State the size-bias identity first for arbitrary theta in [0,m], with m a positive finite mean, and then specialize to the second factorial cumulant when that quantity is available.
findings.impact: Includes the pure double-jump boundary without changing the denominator 1-2*theta or the total variation convention. Removes unnecessary variance and second-moment requirements from the general size-bias identity. No optimality claim or small residual bound is added.

findings.original_assumption: T20.7 is stated for separated primitive regular triples with H=C0*B, C0>1. Its proof bounds singleton free components by an additional defective-vertex estimate, and then bounds components meeting exactly two blocks by pi(H)+2 for each pair.
findings.finding: Under local even-map injectivity and pairwise directness, all free components missing one specified block, including singletons, number at most pi(H)+2. Their component coefficients inject into the actual small-prime coordinates and the two remaining block parities. Consequently dim(R_D)<=c3(D)+3*(pi(H)+2) holds as a finite bound, with no defective-vertex estimate. This needs only H>=B and positive windows starting at least two; no physical separation is needed. The critical-band conclusion therefore includes C0=1 and overlapping triples under the retained injectivity/directness hypotheses.
findings.proposed_revision: Group every unpinned component missing one of the three blocks, including isolated components, under the same small-prime and two-parity rank argument. State the finite bound dim(R_D)<=c3(D)+3*pi(H)+6. Permit H>=B, and omit separation when the stated local injectivity and pairwise directness are retained; the original fixed-ratio conclusion then includes C0=1.
findings.impact: Removes the separate defect-count term and its asymptotic input from this rank comparison, gives an explicit finite bound and weakens the separation/cutoff hypotheses. The full three-block relation space need not be direct. No primitive-host count, mass estimate or optimality claim is added.

findings.original_assumption: T19.6 assumes fixed 0<c<sqrt(13)/4 and uses a smooth-pair estimate attributed to Pascadi; with the de la Breteche--Drappeau input the stated range is c<2/sqrt(5). The threshold is ceil(ceil(N/L)*exp(-c*sqrt(log N*log log N))).
findings.finding: Uniform actual branching through K*(log N)^2 old windows gives F_k<=(2*N^(3/4+epsilon))^k. Choosing epsilon=1/20 and k=ceil(128*(log N)^2) proves P(Z_N>b)<=exp(-2*(log N)^3) for every b>=N^(9/10), and the source truncated-moment bound uniformly for integer 0<=r<=log N. The literal source threshold exceeds N^(9/10) for every fixed c>0, so its upper restriction on c and its smooth-pair analytic input can both be removed.
findings.proposed_revision: Replace the analytic smooth-pair and dependency-graph proof of T19.6 with the uniform quartic logarithmic prime-budget argument, actual distinct-tuple recurrence, and growing-order falling-factorial Markov bound. State the stronger power threshold N^(9/10), then deduce the original rounded near-linear thresholds for every fixed c>0.
findings.impact: A strictly smaller threshold, a stronger probability exponent and no smooth-pair literature input. One N threshold controls all critical lengths and all moment orders through log N. This does not supply bounded low-order moments or the main Poisson approximation.

findings.original_assumption: T19.5 chooses K=K(C,D,r). Its proof invokes the growing-order estimate of T19.4, which is initialized by F_2=O_C(1) from the pair estimate.
findings.finding: The same literal threshold and both truncated-moment conclusions follow from an actual factorial recurrence initialized at F_0=1, with no bounded-pair-moment or fixed-order-moment input. Moreover the explicit coefficient K=E+D+r+log 4 is independent of the fixed critical-band width C. The N threshold still depends on C. The power-threshold conclusion has the eventual bound N^(-D), with constant one.
findings.proposed_revision: Give the square logarithmic prime-budget envelope (a*H*h^(1/3))^2 at order ceil(h^(2/3)), start the actual factorial recurrence at F_0=1 and apply the falling-factorial Markov inequality. State the explicit coefficient K=E+D+r+log 4 before choosing C; retain the dependence of the eventual N threshold on C.
findings.impact: Closes the effective support proof independently of bounded second moments, makes the coefficient independent of C and proves the power-threshold bound with constant one. This does not prove the low-order moment asymptotic or T19.4 itself.

findings.original_assumption: Lemma 3.5 is stated for good edges in the leading channels: compatible dependent regular pairs, with private prime coordinates on their distinct normalized values. It gives a rank lower bound with O(1), a width O(B) and B^{O(1)} endpoint patterns.
findings.finding: Finite compression holds for arbitrary positive coprime coefficients a<=b as soon as one normalized value is shared and the distinct normalized values have private parity coordinates. Affine compatibility, dependence, physical separation and a prior local-regularity assumption are unnecessary. Private coordinates already imply both local ranks equal L. The actual compressed rank is |U|-1 and at least (2-1/b)*L-1. There are at most (L+1)^2 fixed integer motifs, all in [-bL,bL]; one fixed-pattern integer anchor determines both centres.
findings.proposed_revision: State the finite compression for positive coprime coefficients a<=b, a shared normalized value and private coordinates, and then specialize to good edges. Replace the unspecified finite losses and offset count by rank >=(2-1/b)*L-1 and at most (L+1)^2 motifs in [-bL,bL]. State explicitly that the anchor determines both centres and that local regularity follows from the private-coordinate condition.
findings.impact: Gives explicit finite constants and patterns, extends the compression beyond compatible dependent separated pairs and makes the deduplication and single-parameter assertion precise. For fixed a,b the width remains logarithmic. No good-edge count, mass asymptotic or optimality claim is added.

findings.original_assumption: T2.6 gives the universal coefficient bound gamma_{a:b}<=2/3, with a finite numerator range and an implicit denominator restriction through b/2<c/d<2a. It does not supply an admissible channel attaining 2/3.
findings.finding: The denominator range is explicitly bounded by d<=2*b*(a+b-1), with exact equivalence to the displayed source conditions. The literal finite coefficient has gamma_2:3=1/3, gamma_3:4=1/2 and gamma_8:9=2/3. In channel 8:9 the admissible fraction c/d=6/1 has gcds 2 and 3, so its density is 2/3. Thus the universal ceiling is sharp for the defined finite density coefficient across admissible fixed channels.
findings.proposed_revision: Add the explicit denominator cutoff to the computable definition, record the exact leading-channel values and the example gamma_8:9=2/3, and state that sharpness here concerns the displayed finite density coefficient. Keep actual rank-loss and Palm-exponent optimality as separate questions.
findings.impact: Makes the finite enumeration literal and proves that its universal constant cannot be reduced without altering the coefficient or the channel class. This establishes only the coefficient part of T2.6, not its aligned-target rank estimate or the sharpness of an actual arithmetic rank loss.

findings.original_assumption: The proofs of T2.6 and T1.11 bound the union of the two affine matching residue classes by B*(gcd(c,a)+gcd(c,b)-1)/c+O(1). The finite error and the intersection class are left implicit.
findings.finding: For every integer interval [lo,hi), every integer shift h and natural coprime a,b and c,d with c>0, the actual union of c/gcd(c,a) | h+d*k and c/gcd(c,b) | h+d*k has absolute error at most 3 from (hi-lo)*(gcd(c,a)+gcd(c,b)-1)/c. The intersection is exactly the class modulo c. The bound is uniform with no height restriction. Consequently the nonphysical interior window counts are <=B*gamma+3, including all numerators beyond the finite gamma cutoff, and specialize to B/3+3 and B/2+3 in the leading channels.
findings.proposed_revision: Insert the finite affine residue-class lemma before the asymptotic rank argument, with the exact intersection modulus and absolute error at most 3. Keep the bridge from actual old/new value matches and the residual-rank estimate as distinct steps, and retain the separate physical fractions.
findings.impact: Gives an explicit two-sided finite remainder uniform in every integer parameter, with literal window length B=L+1 and no height extrapolation. It proves a divisibility-class count, not equality with an actual rank loss; T2.6 and T1.11 remain in_progress. No optimality claim for the error constant is made.

findings.original_assumption: The proofs of T2.6 and T1.11 use B*gamma+O(1) for actual normalized target matches and B/b+O(1) in the two physical fractions, with the true-window and compatibility bridges left implicit.
findings.finding: For positive coprime a<b with b>=3, every reduced strict-interior target fraction c/d has at most B*gamma_{a:b}+3 actual matching positions, provided the two actual source labels are a*t,b*t and the target is distinct from each source with positive actual joint mass. The physical cases c=a,d=1 and c=b,d=1 have the sharper bound B/b+2. Only the deduplicated normalized source union is used. The result is finite and has no height cutoff; a good edge supplies a positive integer source parameter.
findings.proposed_revision: Insert the exact actual-match set and its injection into the two affine classes. Derive at-most-one raw overlap from positive joint start mass, and state B/b+2 for physical fractions and B*gamma+3 for the combined finite bound. Retain the residual normalized rank and endpoint arguments as separate steps.
findings.impact: Closes the actual-value and physical-window bridges in T2.6/T1.11 without substituting a containing interval for the true source set. These are position counts, not a completed rank-loss or Palm estimate. Both numbered statements remain in_progress; no optimality claim for the finite additive constants is made.

findings.original_assumption: T1.9 states the uniform aligned-pair rank estimate for separated aligned windows of reduced height at most B^3. The residual argument gives no explicit finite bound.
findings.finding: One actual normalized coincidence suffices for the uniform full pair deficiency bound <=(u-1)+epsilon*B. With positive coprime a<=b and b<=B^3 it is also <=L/b+epsilon*B. The common critical-band threshold is chosen before every channel and pair. Separation, affine compatibility and local regularity are unnecessary for these assertions. The full pair deficiency includes internal local rank defects and dominates the actual intersection rank. A finite residual bound on any true subset S of two dilated intervals is max(r+1,2*t*2^((r+1)/t+1))+|S|/(K+1), with strict inequality and r the literal omitted-prime count, under (64R)^(2Kt)<U.
findings.proposed_revision: State the one-unit uniform rank assertion independently of separation and compatibility. Give the finite Runge--Hamming component bound, including the exact K+1 large-component budget and the omitted primes dividing the coefficients. Keep the final fixed-height enlarged-cutoff rate as a separate assertion.
findings.impact: Closes the uniform o(B) part of T1.9 on actual normalized values and proves a stronger bound including internal deficiencies. The arithmetic residual estimate is proved on true subsets and for polynomial-height coefficients. At this initial validation checkpoint the fixed-height enlarged-cutoff assertion and the target quotient-rank and endpoint bridges were separate unfinished work. Later numbered-result completion is tracked independently in the source coverage ledger.
